newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Former South Korean banker jailed for corruption.
newsitem.headline: Former South Korean banker jailed for corruption.

text.p: A former head of a leading South Korean bank was jailed for three years on Thursday for taking bribes in return for loans to a local valve company, a Seoul court judge said.
The sentencing came as a string of local bankers were probed in a loan scandal surrounding now-insolvent Hanbo Steel Co, the nation's second largest steelmaker.
Sohn Hong-kyun, former president of SEOULBANK, was also fined 160 million won ($184,000), the amount of commission he took from the company last year, judge Nam Jung-in said.

State prosecutors said Sohn accepted bank accounts under the name of the valve company's executive and registered seals to cover up illegal deals. Banks use registered seals in South Korea as well as signatures to authorise transactions.
"The commission Sohn received was so large that he deserved three years in prison," said Nam.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate, defaulted on debt repayments on January 23 after piling up five trillion won in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.

Two bankers were arrested on Wednesday on charges of taking 400 million won in kickbacks in exchange for huge loans to Hanbo. Two other leading bankers were being questioned by prosecutors on Thursday over the Hanbo crisis.
SEOULBANK is one of South Korea's seven largest banks in terms of deposits.
